extracted.intended_audience: foreign applicants, in-house counsel, and patent practitioners seeking to file and prosecute patents (EAPO/OAPI/PCT/WIPO) in regional jurisdictions
extracted.subtask_description: Practical and procedural guidance for filing, prosecuting, and maintaining patents and industrial designs via the Eurasian Patent Office (EAPO), with related notes on OAPI, WIPO/PCT, and regional filing strategy. Covers filing languages, deadlines, fees, examination requests, representation, PCT regional phase, and maintenance considerations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Single Eurasian application for multi-state protection
rubrics_metrics.description: The EAPO provides intellectual property protection for inventions and industrial designs through a single Eurasian application that is valid in all eight member states.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This system simplifies the application process, reducing costs and saving time by allowing applicants to protect ideas in multiple countries with one procedure; after grant, the patent owner can choose in which member states to maintain the patent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Filing language and Russian translation deadline
rubrics_metrics.description: A Eurasian application can be submitted in any language but must be followed by a Russian translation within two months, or within four months if the applicant pays an extra fee.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure timely submission of the Russian translation to avoid procedural complications; consider paying the extra fee only if additional time is needed.

rubrics_metrics.name: EAPO PCT regional phase entry deadline
rubrics_metrics.description: A Eurasian patent can be obtained based on a PCT application by entering the Eurasian regional phase within 31 months from the earliest priority date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Observe the 31‑month deadline for regional phase entry when using a PCT route to secure the option of a Eurasian patent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Request for substantive examination (timing)
rubrics_metrics.description: All Eurasian patent applications go through a thorough examination. For regular applications, the applicant must request this examination within six months after the publication of the search report.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For PCT-based applications the request must be made when entering the regional phase. Track publication dates and regional-phase entry timing so examination requests are not missed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fees paid to EAPO and fee reduction rules
rubrics_metrics.description: All fees related to Eurasian patents or industrial designs are paid directly to the EAPO. The filing fee may be reduced by 25 percent if the application includes an international or PCT search report from another authorized office; the fee can be reduced by 40 percent if the report was produced by the Eurasian Patent Office.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider obtaining an appropriate search report (e.g., PCT ISR) or using EAPO search to benefit from reduced official fees; budget accordingly and submit qualifying reports with the filing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exclusive rights between publication and first annual fee
rubrics_metrics.description: Between the time the patent is published and the payment of the first annual fee, the patent owner holds exclusive rights to their invention across all member states.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be aware of this protection window and the obligation to pay the first annuity to maintain rights; plan commercialization and enforcement actions with this timing in mind.

rubrics_metrics.name: Post-grant maintenance choices and restoration
rubrics_metrics.description: After a Eurasian patent is granted, the patent owner can choose in which member states they want to maintain the patent. They can also restore patents that lapsed due to unpaid fees.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Select member states for national-level maintenance based on commercial strategy and be prepared to use restoration procedures if fees are missed (subject to local rules and any time limits).

rubrics_metrics.name: Patent term extension eligibility (certain inventions)
rubrics_metrics.description: In some cases, the owner may extend the validity of the patent for specific types of inventions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Particularly in regulated sectors (e.g., pharmaceuticals/biotech), assess eligibility for term extensions and prepare supporting documentation; extensions require jurisdictional assessment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirement for local representative (EAPO)
rubrics_metrics.description: A registered Eurasian patent attorney is required for foreign applicants.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Engage a local/registered Eurasian patent attorney to file and prosecute applications on behalf of foreign applicants; this is mandatory for EAPO filings.

rubrics_metrics.name: EAPO as PCT International Authority (ISA/IPEA)
rubrics_metrics.description: Since 2022, the EAPO has also served as an international search authority and an international preliminary examination authority under the PCT system.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants may be able to obtain PCT search and preliminary examination reports from EAPO where applicable; consider this when choosing receiving office or search authority.

rubrics_metrics.name: Participation in Patent Prosecution Highway (PPH) programs
rubrics_metrics.description: The EAPO participates in Patent Prosecution Highway programs with several intellectual property offices worldwide (e.g., Chinese Patent Office, KIPO, Finnish PRH).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use PPH routes to potentially speed up examination by sharing examination results between offices; verify bilateral/multilateral PPH eligibility and procedural requirements before relying on accelerated routes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use case guidance: when EAPO is not the best choice
rubrics_metrics.description: If you only need protection in one member country, or your key market is outside the EAPO member states, a national filing (or a different regional route) can be more targeted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Map actual sales/manufacturing countries first, then choose the route that best matches commercial footprint to avoid unnecessary costs and maintenance obligations.

rubrics_metrics.name: OAPI centralized system covers all member states
rubrics_metrics.description: OAPI provides a single application process that grants IP protection in all member states; owing to the fact that all OAPI member states are governed by the Bangui Agreement, it is not possible to designate certain member states for IP protection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Filing via OAPI means a registered right is valid in all 17 member states simultaneously—use OAPI when you want broad Francophone African coverage; plan accordingly because you cannot opt out of individual states.

rubrics_metrics.name: OAPI filing strategy advice
rubrics_metrics.description: If your target markets are largely within OAPI's 17 member states, OAPI's centralized system can be an efficient route; if your plan includes non-OAPI African states, you may need a mixed strategy (OAPI + national and/or another regional route).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess market coverage needs and combine routes where necessary to cover non-OAPI jurisdictions; consider administrative and enforcement implications of a mixed filing strategy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirement for local representative (OAPI)
rubrics_metrics.description: Yes, a registered patent attorney is required for foreign applicants.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Engage a registered agent for OAPI filings to ensure compliance with procedural requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: PCT: single international filing but no 'international patent'
rubrics_metrics.description: The Patent Cooperation Treaty (PCT) enables applicants to file a single patent application, which can then enter national or regional phases to seek protection in up to 158 countries and regions; however, the PCT does not provide a single 'international patent'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the PCT to buy time and streamline initial prosecution, but plan for separate national/regional prosecutions (and fees) when entering designated jurisdictions.

rubrics_metrics.name: PCT national/regional phase entry timing
rubrics_metrics.description: Under the PCT agreement, applicants must transition their applications into the national or regional phases to seek patent protection in specific jurisdictions. This step typically occurs within 30 or 31 months from the earliest priority date, depending on the regulations of each country or region.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Track country-specific national/regional phase deadlines (30 vs 31 months) and prepare translations, national forms, and local representation before the deadline.

rubrics_metrics.name: Independent prosecution in each national/regional jurisdiction
rubrics_metrics.description: During national or regional phases, patent prosecution proceeds independently in each chosen jurisdiction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Expect different examination outcomes and requirements across offices; coordinate with local agents and factor in disparate timelines, office actions, and claim amendments per jurisdiction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Annuities and maintaining patent validity
rubrics_metrics.description: Maintaining patent validity requires the timely payment of annuities in each jurisdiction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Set up annuity management processes to avoid lapse; missed payments can be costly and may require restoration procedures with limits and conditions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patent term extensions in regulated industries
rubrics_metrics.description: In certain industries, such as pharmaceuticals and biotechnology, patents may be eligible for term extensions to compensate for time lost during regulatory approval processes; these extensions can add up to five years to the standard 20-year patent term, depending on specific criteria and jurisdictional regulations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Conduct a thorough eligibility assessment for term extension opportunities and engage experts to pursue extensions where available; rules vary by jurisdiction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Practical budgeting and quotation advice
rubrics_metrics.description: Start with an initial quotation that separates official fees from professional fees, so you can see what is fixed vs what depends on attorney work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use structured estimates (e.g., IP-Coster) to get transparent breakdowns before choosing filing routes; this helps compare EAPO, OAPI, national, and PCT options.
